article_title: Are California voters about to impose world's first tax on billionaires?

tasks.prompt: What central choice does California's Proposition 40 put before voters?
options: Whether to impose a one-time 5% wealth tax on the state's billionaires to support healthcare
Whether to replace state income tax with a national sales tax
Whether to tax all annual income above $1m at 9.9%
Whether to prohibit billionaires from moving to another state
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הצעה 40 מבקשת להטיל מס חד־פעמי של 5% על הונם של מיליארדרים בקליפורניה כדי לממן את מערכת הבריאות.
tasks.correct_answer: Whether to impose a one-time 5% wealth tax on the state's billionaires to support healthcare

tasks.prompt: How much revenue do supporters aim to raise through the measure?
tasks.explanation_hebrew: תומכי ההצעה שואפים לגייס 100 מיליארד דולר כדי להשלים קיצוצים פדרליים במימון הבריאות.

tasks.prompt: Which group would be liable under the proposal if it passes?
options: Anyone earning more than $1m a year
All California residents who own company shares
People worth at least $1bn who lived in California on 1 January 2026
Only technology executives who remain in California in November
tasks.explanation_hebrew: המס יחול רטרואקטיבית על מי ששווי הונו לפחות מיליארד דולר ושגר בקליפורניה ב־1 בינואר 2026.
tasks.correct_answer: People worth at least $1bn who lived in California on 1 January 2026

tasks.prompt: In the article, what does “capital flight” refer to?
options: A government borrowing money abroad
Investors buying airline companies
Workers travelling to a financial centre
Wealth or wealthy residents moving away to avoid costs or taxes
tasks.explanation_hebrew: בהקשר הכלכלי, capital flight הוא יציאה של הון או של בעלי הון ממקום מסוים, בין היתר בגלל מסים.
tasks.correct_answer: Wealth or wealthy residents moving away to avoid costs or taxes

tasks.prompt: Why does Governor Gavin Newsom oppose Proposition 40?
options: He fears it could drive wealthy residents away and reduce future income-tax revenue.
He believes California has too few billionaires for the plan to matter.
He wants the money to fund schools instead of healthcare.
He argues that federal healthcare cuts have already been reversed.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: ניוסם חושש שהמס יעודד עשירים לעזוב וכך יפחית את הכנסות המדינה ממס הכנסה לאורך זמן.
tasks.correct_answer: He fears it could drive wealthy residents away and reduce future income-tax revenue.

tasks.prompt: What did the September poll show about likely voters?
options: A clear two-thirds majority supported the tax.
Most voters were undecided.
Opponents led supporters by 13 points.
Support was 45%, opposition 42%, and 13% were undecided.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הסקר מצא 45% תמיכה, 42% התנגדות ו־13% שטרם החליטו, ולכן לא היה רוב ברור.
tasks.correct_answer: Support was 45%, opposition 42%, and 13% were undecided.

tasks.prompt: Identify two examples the article uses to show that wealth taxes can influence where rich people live or keep their wealth.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להביא שתי דוגמאות מדויקות, מקליפורניה או מההשוואות הבינלאומיות שבכתבה.
expected_points: At least six California billionaires reportedly left before the residency deadline.
Norway saw an unusually large number of very wealthy people leave after a tax increase.
A Swiss study found taxable wealth fell after a wealth-tax increase.
Hankey moved to Nevada and other billionaires discussed or planned leaving.

tasks.prompt: Write a concise summary of the strongest case for Proposition 40 and the strongest case against it.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להציג באופן מאוזן את טיעון המימון והשוויון מצד התומכים ואת טיעון העזיבה, ההשקעות וההכנסות העתידיות מצד המתנגדים.
expected_points: Supporters say the tax would fund healthcare after federal cuts and make the ultra-wealthy contribute more fairly.
Opponents warn of administrative difficulty, reduced investment and wealthy residents leaving.
Departure could shrink California's future income-tax base even if the levy raises money initially.

tasks.prompt: Evaluate how effectively the article uses international evidence from Norway and Switzerland in the California debate. What can the evidence show, and what can it not prove?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להעריך את הרלוונטיות והמגבלות: הדוגמאות מחזקות חשש לשינוי התנהגות, אך אינן מוכיחות שתוצאה זהה תתרחש בקליפורניה.
expected_points: Norway provides evidence of wealthy people leaving after a tax increase.
The Swiss study links a higher wealth-tax rate with lower taxable wealth.
Different laws, economies and tax designs limit direct prediction for California.
The evidence supports a risk, not certainty about Proposition 40's outcome.

tasks.prompt: Write a brief editorial arguing whether voters should support Proposition 40. Address healthcare funding, fairness and the risk of wealthy residents leaving.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: המאמר צריך להציג עמדה ברורה, לשלב לפחות שלושה פרטים מדויקים מן הכתבה ולהתייחס ברצינות לטיעון הנגדי.
expected_points: States a clear position on Proposition 40.
Uses evidence about the 5% levy, the $100bn goal or healthcare funding cuts.
Discusses fairness or California's wealth gap.
Addresses capital flight and possible loss of income-tax revenue.
